Astroray · 24–27 September 2026 · overnight run report

Astroray Night Shift

Three nights, eight batches, and a lot of light that had been going missing. The renderer now agrees with Cycles in places it used to argue: dispersive glass, fire, the setting sun, thin films on metal, lamps inside fog. Along the way it learned about Kerr black holes and physically honest photons. The PC rebooted itself twice, which we are choosing to read as applause.

The short version

Everything on the 2026-09-24 plan shipped: Batches U, V, Y (light transport, viewport, procedural textures), the GR pair pkg281/282, and the owner's showcase scenes. The showcase then did its real job, which was to find bugs: six of them, all now fixed. After the queue ran dry, a Fable architect run (the one exception you allowed) triaged 53 open issues and wrote ten specs; Batches AD and AE came straight out of that plan. The last batch (AE, photon caustics) passed the full suite with zero failures and is merged.

One thing did not land: the clamp-parity package (pkg290) is blocked, honestly. Its real cause is that light sampling inside fog is 100–500× noisier than Cycles, which is now issue #925 and the most valuable item on the next plan.

The showcase, and what it caught

You asked for glass dispersion with caustics, volumes, a Nishita sun and thin film on metal. Four scenes, 1920×1080, Astroray on the GPU against Cycles on OptiX. The first previews were humbling. Here is where they ended up.

The glass scene, before and after the caustic work

Same scene, same 4096 samples, same GPU. The rainbow fan loses its salt-and-pepper, the refracted beam on the floor goes smooth, and the ball's caustic stops being confetti. A few white fireflies remain around the prism: those are sun reflections off the glass, which are still path traced rather than carried by photons.

The speckle under the ball had three separate causes (#909): every one of 4096 samples reused the same photon map, the gather radius collapsed near lonely photons, and caustics were counted twice (once as photons, once by path tracing). Batch AE then made the photons physical (pkg286) and gave every lamp type its own photons (pkg287). A spot lamp's caustic now matches brute-force path tracing:

Batch by batch

Z: glass, sky, soap bubbles and a spinning black hole

Dispersive glass had been losing three quarters of its light. When a Sellmeier refraction collapses the four wavelengths to one, pbrt divides that wavelength's pdf by four; we zeroed the others and forgot the division. One line, 4× brighter, and the prism fringes finally look like a prism.

The sunset sky had two faults: its glow was baked 90° away from the sun, and the sun disc was a lamp that camera rays skip. Metallic thin films were shifted 70 nm thin by a sign in the interference phase (invisible on glass, where the reflection phase is 0 or π). And the black hole now spins: the reference-bank image was re-blessed on the Kerr engine and checked against GYOTO.

AB: the pole, the fire, and caustics that average

Rays that grazed the black hole's spin axis stalled in Boyer–Lindquist coordinates, ran out of steps and were declared swallowed. Near the pole the integrator now switches to Kerr–Schild coordinates (the GRay2 approach).

The fire was a third too dim because Astroray clamped Blackbody Intensity to 1 while Cycles takes it as given (the scene uses 3).

pkg283 gave the ADAF and jet emission models proper relativistic transport: 59 analytic tests, and the jet lost a Doppler factor it never deserved.

AC: the CPU was the one lying

With several lamps inside fog the GPU rendered 13–21 % brighter than the CPU. We assumed the GPU. It was the CPU: when a scattered ray hit one emitter, its MIS weight also counted every emitter hiding behind it (#912). Separately, an "intermittent crash" in the caustic tests turned out to be GCC on Windows emitting aligned AVX stores to a stack it cannot align (GCC bug 54412). One assembler flag: 22 of 36 runs crashing became 50 of 50 clean.

AD: lamps you can see past

A ray that hit a lamp used to stop there, so a wall behind a lamp, seen in a mirror, came out at 6 % brightness. Paths now continue through lamps, as in Cycles. The SMS energy statistic read −140,000 because converged points facing the wrong way produced negative Fresnel terms (one reviewer insisted the fix was backwards; the caustic energy measurement disagreed). ReSTIR's blue suns came from lamps converting their colour to RGB with the path's own four wavelengths and back again.

One test failure turned out to be the test: the raindrop-bow check had been grading adaptive-sampling tile noise and passed by luck at exactly its threshold. With adaptive sampling off, the bow is bit-identical before and after, and very much a bow.

AE: photons with honest energy, and a finding about fog

Photons now carry real flux. A glass slab under a sun transmits 0.926 against the analytic 0.922, and doubling the sun doubles the caustic to three decimals. Two more energy bugs fell out: photon deposits were multiplied by the receiver's cosine a second time, and glass-to-air exits ignored total internal reflection.

The fog-shaft speckle (#913) was not a colour problem at all. Astroray samples lamps only at the rare points where light actually scatters; Cycles samples a lamp connection on every stretch of fog. Same average, very different noise:

Per-pixel normalised variance at 64 spp, 12 seeds, log scale. A strict expected-failure test now pins this gap, so the fix (#925) has to turn it green.

Tests, and keeping them honest

The suite grew by 317 tests across the batches, and every batch was run in full on the RTX 5070 Ti before its PR.

Your rule from Friday (a test calibrated on a broken engine gets fixed, never obeyed) got a real workout. Tests re-pinned because they encoded old bugs:

  • Three dispersion gates that required dispersion to darken the glass (that darkening was #901).
  • Eight sky-orientation checks tuned with the glow in the wrong place.
  • The Kerr reference image, rendered back when spin was ignored.
  • A clamp test that measured the edge of a lamp instead of the clamp; a photon-seed test that single-map averaging made obsolete; the raindrop bow.

GPU register budget

The shade kernel stays pinned at 254 registers with no new spills. The intersect stage absorbed the lamp pass-through loop, so it grew; nothing spills.

What went sideways

  • Two hard resets (Windows Kernel-Power 41, no bugcheck) while the GPU suite, CUDA builds and several busy lanes ran at once. That points to a power or thermal trip, not software. Since the second: one heavy job at a time, at most two CPU lanes, 8 threads, -j 6. No resets since.
  • The second reset left four source files in one worktree as pure NUL bytes. Work continued in a fresh worktree; the damaged one (Astroray-f912) is untouched for you to delete.
  • The cheap reviewer ran out of tokens on large diffs four times; splitting the diff fixed it every time. One delegated edit came back as a corrupted binary file and was discarded.
  • The architect's clamp package (pkg290) is blocked, with evidence: neither proposed metric closes the gap, because the gap is sampling noise (#922, #925).

Next up

#925 is already half done: the CPU now samples a light connection on every stretch of fog (lit-shaft noise from ~100× Cycles down to 2–7×), and the new unbiasedness test caught and fixed an older bias for lamps inside fog boxes. The GPU half is #929. After that the architect's order continues with the GPU/CPU divergence ladders (pkg292, pkg293), then the new parity corpus and the reference-bank re-bless once the transport fixes stop moving pixels.
